rule: local-dev onboarding bypass gate and fixture identity

fixture_identity.notes: A single non-privileged, never-pricing-seeded uid reused across every platform. It carries no Stripe/subscription document, so it resolves to Free/no-entitlement through the same code path as any brand-new never-subscribed account — no plan-specific fixture wiring needed. It is distinct from the pricing_* fixtures (scripts/dev-harness/PRICING_SCENARIOS.md) — see identity_semantics for how those compose with this bypass.

gate_semantics.description: The bypass is active only when BOTH an explicit local-dev profile/config gate AND a SEPARATE explicit bypass flag are set. Neither condition alone is sufficient. The bypass must never be inferred from build type (debug/release), persisted state (a prior onboarding-complete flag), or merely having an existing signed-in session — it requires the flag to be truthy on THIS run, and the signed-in identity must match fixture_identity.uid before onboarding is treated as satisfied.
gate_semantics.disable_path: Unset (or set to any value other than "1") the bypass flag; the local-dev profile/config gate may remain set. A fresh run then falls back to the platform's normal manual local-dev sign-in (still profile-gated) and onboarding is not skipped.

identity_semantics.description: Onboarding is treated as satisfied when the bypass is active (gate_semantics above) AND the signed-in uid is either the fixture_identity.uid OR any uid carrying the pricing_uid_prefix below (the seeded pricing QA fixtures — scripts/dev-harness/PRICING_SCENARIOS.md — e.g. pricing_plus, pricing_unlimited_v2). This is a prefix rule, not an enumerated list: the harness seeds pricing fixtures dynamically per scenario (scripts/dev-harness/dev_harness/pricing_scenarios.py), so a fixed list would drift. A uid is never treated as satisfying onboarding merely because the bypass flag is set — the identity check always runs too, and a uid outside both categories (e.g. a real Google/Apple-signed-in account, or 'alice') still runs the real onboarding wizard even with the flag on.
identity_semantics.macos_pricing_prefix_skip_is_a_separate_: macOS's pricing_* onboarding-skip is unconditional on the local_dev harness profile alone (scripts/dev-harness/dev_harness/desktop_profile.py's _is_pricing_harness_launch sets OMI_SKIP_ONBOARDING=1 for any pricing_-prefixed launch uid, decided before the app even starts) — it predates this bypass and does not read this bypass's flag at all. Windows and mobile have no launch-time hook (their local-dev sign-in is typed at runtime in a running app), so they gate the SAME pricing_* identity rule behind this bypass's flag instead, by user decision (2026-09-07): keeps the flag-off path able to still exercise the real onboarding wizard against a preset pricing uid on those two platforms.
